patch.value: A truncated list-all answer is consumed as if it were the whole workspace

Both list-all readers take .items and act on it as if it were everything. readPmItemsForUpsert builds the upsert key index, and fetchPmItems feeds the TODO export. Neither consults the completeness receipt the envelope has carried since 2026.8.15. Under pm-cli 2026.8.14 the same calls returned 10 items of a 682-item workspace with truncated true, so the upsert index missed keys and created duplicates while the exporter wrote a TODO file missing 98 percent of its rows, both reporting success. Two aggravating factors found alongside it: readPmItemsForUpsert passed a hardcoded limit of 10000 rows, which with a completeness gate in place converts every larger workspace from a big read into a hard refusal of upsert, and fetchPmItems passed no maxBuffer at all, so an overrun kills the child with a null status and empty stderr and surfaces as an unattributable pm list-all failed.

assertListAllComplete refuses an envelope carrying any of truncated, has_more, a completeness.status other than complete (an absent receipt included), or omission_receipt.has_omissions, naming the tripped signal, the count-versus-total scale, and which operation was refused. Both readers call it. The hardcoded limit of 10000 is removed from the upsert read and fetchPmItems now passes a maxBuffer and classifies the ENOBUFS case. The CLI is exact-pinned at 2026.8.15 with a >=2026.8.15 peer floor.

A truncated or degraded envelope aborts the upsert or the export with a message naming the signal, instead of building a key index that creates duplicates or writing a TODO file missing most of its rows.

153 of 153 tests pass, up from 146. Neutering assertListAllComplete fails 5 of them. The seven new cases are driven from a real 2026.8.15 envelope captured from the CLI against a live two-item workspace with exactly one field mutated per case, including the bare-array case that carries no receipt and must not be refused.
